Missing data

Source: vignettes/missing-data.Rmd
missing-data.Rmd
library(sRtr)

SRTR variables record missing information in many ways, and the codes differ from variable to variable. Code 4 is “Unknown” in one format, “N/A” in another and “Not tested” in a third. sRtr handles this in three steps that can be used separately:

  1. missing_codes says what each code means.
  2. srtr_missing_report() counts what is in your data.
  3. srtr_normalize_missing() turns the kinds you choose into NA.

The rows below are made up. They use column names from TX_KI.

tx_ki <- data.frame(
  DON_ANTI_HCV = c("P", "N", "U", "ND", "I", "PD"),
  DON_HIST_DIAB = c(1, 5, 998, 998, 2, NA),
  CAN_MALIG = c("Y", "N", "U", "", "ND", "N")
)

With real data, load_srtr_file("TX_KI") records the dataset on the data frame, so file_key does not need to be given.

What the codes mean

missing_codes$formats classifies the format codes that may stand for missing information. Each code has one type.

codes <- missing_codes$formats
codes[codes$Format == "SRLSTT", c("Code", "Meaning", "missing_type")]
#>     Code            Meaning    missing_type
#> 234    C C: Cannot Disclose cannot_disclose
#> 235    I   I: Indeterminate   indeterminate
#> 236   ND       ND: Not Done        not_done
#> 237   PD        PD: Pending         pending
#> 238    U         U: Unknown         unknown

The types are unknown, not_applicable, not_done, pending, cannot_disclose, indeterminate, partial (part of the answer is known, such as “Yes, duration unknown”), sas_missing and none (an ordinary value). They are sRtr’s grouping of the meanings in the SRTR data dictionary, not an SRTR classification.

missing_codes$variables covers flag columns that have no format, with values such as a blank, U or ND. The SRTR dictionary does not document these values; they are listed from experience with the files.

What is in the data

srtr_missing_report() counts the codes by type and changes nothing.

srtr_missing_report(tx_ki, file_key = "TX_KI")
#> # A tibble: 10 × 5
#>    variable      format  missing_type      n percent
#>    <chr>         <chr>   <chr>         <int>   <dbl>
#>  1 DON_ANTI_HCV  SRLSTT  unknown           1    16.7
#>  2 DON_ANTI_HCV  SRLSTT  not_done          1    16.7
#>  3 DON_ANTI_HCV  SRLSTT  pending           1    16.7
#>  4 DON_ANTI_HCV  SRLSTT  indeterminate     1    16.7
#>  5 DON_HIST_DIAB HSTDBDR unknown           2    33.3
#>  6 DON_HIST_DIAB HSTDBDR partial           1    16.7
#>  7 DON_HIST_DIAB HSTDBDR na                1    16.7
#>  8 CAN_MALIG     NA      unknown           1    16.7
#>  9 CAN_MALIG     NA      not_done          1    16.7
#> 10 CAN_MALIG     NA      sas_missing       1    16.7

detail = "code" lists every classified code with its count, including codes that do not occur.

srtr_missing_report(
  tx_ki,
  cols = "DON_ANTI_HCV",
  file_key = "TX_KI",
  detail = "code"
)
#> # A tibble: 5 × 7
#>   variable     format code  meaning            missing_type        n percent
#>   <chr>        <chr>  <chr> <chr>              <chr>           <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 DON_ANTI_HCV SRLSTT U     U: Unknown         unknown             1    16.7
#> 2 DON_ANTI_HCV SRLSTT ND    ND: Not Done       not_done            1    16.7
#> 3 DON_ANTI_HCV SRLSTT PD    PD: Pending        pending             1    16.7
#> 4 DON_ANTI_HCV SRLSTT C     C: Cannot Disclose cannot_disclose     0     0  
#> 5 DON_ANTI_HCV SRLSTT I     I: Indeterminate   indeterminate       1    16.7

Choosing what becomes NA

By default, srtr_normalize_missing() uses the "analysis" policy.

srtr_normalize_missing(tx_ki, file_key = "TX_KI")
#>   DON_ANTI_HCV DON_HIST_DIAB CAN_MALIG
#> 1            P             1         Y
#> 2            N             5         N
#> 3         <NA>            NA      <NA>
#> 4         <NA>            NA      <NA>
#> 5            I             2      <NA>
#> 6         <NA>            NA         N

Unknown, not done, pending, withheld and blank values became NA. “Indeterminate” and the partly known diabetes code were kept, because they say something about the patient.

Once they are NA, “unknown” and “not done” look the same. To keep the difference, ask for reason columns: reason = "changed" adds a _MISS column for each variable that changed, recording why each value became NA.

srtr_normalize_missing(tx_ki, reason = "changed", file_key = "TX_KI")
#>   DON_ANTI_HCV DON_HIST_DIAB CAN_MALIG DON_ANTI_HCV_MISS DON_HIST_DIAB_MISS
#> 1            P             1         Y              <NA>               <NA>
#> 2            N             5         N              <NA>               <NA>
#> 3         <NA>            NA      <NA>           unknown            unknown
#> 4         <NA>            NA      <NA>          not_done            unknown
#> 5            I             2      <NA>              <NA>               <NA>
#> 6         <NA>            NA         N           pending               <NA>
#>   CAN_MALIG_MISS
#> 1           <NA>
#> 2           <NA>
#> 3        unknown
#> 4    sas_missing
#> 5       not_done
#> 6           <NA>

Which kinds of missing value to drop depends on the analysis. Three policies cover common choices:

Kind "analysis" "strict" "tag_only"
unknown, pending, cannot disclose, blank NA NA kept
not done, not tested NA NA kept
not applicable kept NA kept
indeterminate kept NA kept
partly known kept NA kept

"strict" leaves only substantive values. "tag_only" changes no value and adds a reason column for each variable that holds a recognised code.

Adjusting a policy

A test that was not done can be informative in itself. To keep “not done” as a value everywhere:

srtr_normalize_missing(
  tx_ki,
  actions = c(not_done = "keep"),
  file_key = "TX_KI"
)
#>   DON_ANTI_HCV DON_HIST_DIAB CAN_MALIG
#> 1            P             1         Y
#> 2            N             5         N
#> 3         <NA>            NA      <NA>
#> 4           ND            NA      <NA>
#> 5            I             2        ND
#> 6         <NA>            NA         N

To change the rule for one variable only:

srtr_normalize_missing(
  tx_ki,
  overrides = list(DON_ANTI_HCV = c(indeterminate = "na")),
  file_key = "TX_KI"
)
#>   DON_ANTI_HCV DON_HIST_DIAB CAN_MALIG
#> 1            P             1         Y
#> 2            N             5         N
#> 3         <NA>            NA      <NA>
#> 4         <NA>            NA      <NA>
#> 5         <NA>             2      <NA>
#> 6         <NA>            NA         N

Other choices

  • output = "append" leaves the original columns as they are and adds the normalized values in _NORM columns.
  • na_level = "Missing" makes missing its own group in factor and character columns, which is useful for descriptive tables.
  • extra_codes adds your own codes, for example extra_codes = list(MY_VAR = c("9" = "unknown")).
srtr_normalize_missing(
  tx_ki,
  cols = "CAN_MALIG",
  na_level = "Missing",
  file_key = "TX_KI"
)
#>   DON_ANTI_HCV DON_HIST_DIAB CAN_MALIG
#> 1            P             1         Y
#> 2            N             5         N
#> 3            U           998   Missing
#> 4           ND           998   Missing
#> 5            I             2   Missing
#> 6           PD            NA         N

What this does not cover

A blank can mean that a field was not collected in that era, and a continuous variable can hold an implausible value or a placeholder such as 999. Neither is a coded missing value, and srtr_normalize_missing() does not look for them.
